Now let me compile the verse-by-verse notes from all the sources gathered. Here is the full commentary on Revelation 9:

---

## Revelation 9 — Verse-by-Verse Commentary

### v. 1 — The Fifth Trumpet and the Fallen Star

**Traditional Reading:** The "star" is not a literal astronomical body but a person — an angelic being. The perfect-tense Greek participle (*peptōkota*, "having fallen") indicates John saw a star already in a fallen state, not one in the act of falling. Most traditional interpreters identify this star as Satan himself (based on Isaiah 14:12 and Luke 10:18), though some argue it could be a lesser fallen angel. The key to the Abyss is *given* to him — he has no independent authority. The Abyss (*abussos*) is the temporary prison for certain demons (Luke 8:31; 2 Peter 2:4; Jude 6). Precept Austin notes that later an angel will use the same key to lock Satan in the Abyss during the Millennium (Rev. 20:1–2). [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/) | [https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary)

**Baptist (John MacArthur, GTY):** MacArthur explicitly identifies the star as Satan — his "second fall." Satan's first fall was his expulsion from holy service, but he retained access to heaven as accuser (Job 1; Rev. 12:10). During the Tribulation he is thrown down to earth entirely (Rev. 12:7–9), losing all heavenly access. The key is given to him by God's sovereign permission; Christ holds the ultimate keys of death and Hades (Rev. 1:18). [https://www.gty.org/sermons/81-179/unleashing-hell-on-earth](https://www.gty.org/sermons/81-179/unleashing-hell-on-earth)

**Older Baptist (Gill):** Gill interprets the star as the Pope of Rome (the Western Antichrist) or Mahomet (the Eastern Antichrist), applying a historicist reading: the star "fell" when Pope Boniface III received the title of universal bishop from Emperor Phocas (c. AD 606). The key of the bottomless pit represents the papal claim to power over heaven, earth, and hell, symbolized by the triple crown. [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm)

**Anglican (Pulpit Commentary):** The Pulpit Commentary sees the star as Satan, noting that in Numbers 24:17 a star signifies a person in high position, and Revelation 1:20 identifies stars as angels. Isaiah 14:12 ("How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer") clinches the identification. The trumpets now shift from judgments on the outer man to spiritual afflictions emanating directly from the devil. [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/9-1.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/9-1.htm)

**Anglican (Ellicott):** Ellicott likewise sees the fallen star as an evil power — Satan or a great evil ruler. The star is *fallen*, not falling, and is given the key to the Abyss. Ellicott compares the imagery to Dante's *Inferno*, with its narrowing circles winding down to a central shaft. The abyss is the "lowest spring of evil." [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/9.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/revelation/9.htm)

---

### v. 2 — Opening of the Abyss and Darkening Smoke

**Traditional Reading:** When the Abyss is opened, a great plume of smoke rises "like the smoke of a great furnace," darkening the sun and air. This is yet another cosmic disturbance in the Tribulation sequence. Precept Austin connects this smoke to the "pillars of smoke" Joel prophesied for the Day of the Lord (Joel 2:30) and to the smoke that rose from Sodom's destruction (Gen. 19:28). The furnace-like smoke suggests the great heat of the subterranean Abyss, consistent with the rich man's torment "in this flame" (Luke 16:24). [https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary)

**Baptist (MacArthur):** MacArthur describes this as demons "belching out of hell like smoke coming out of a fire pit," blackening the entire environment. The physical devastations of the first four trumpets (on land, sea, fresh water, and sky) now give way to spiritual devastation — a direct demonic assault. [https://www.gty.org/sermons/81-179/unleashing-hell-on-earth](https://www.gty.org/sermons/81-179/unleashing-hell-on-earth)

**Older Baptist (Gill):** In Gill's historicist scheme, the smoke represents false doctrine and superstitious worship arising from papal decrees and Mahomet's Koran. "Christ, the sun of righteousness, was greatly obscured by the Romish antichrist." The darkening describes how the light of the gospel was beclouded by medieval corruption. [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm)

---

### v. 3 — Locusts from the Smoke

**Traditional Reading:** These are demonic beings, not natural locusts, as proven by subsequent verses (they do not eat vegetation; they have a king). The imagery recalls the Egyptian plague (Ex. 10:12–15), but with a crucial difference: these target people, not crops. Enduring Word and Precept Austin both note Joel 2:1–11 as a key parallel, where an end-time "army of the Lord" is described in locust-like terms. God controls even this demonic horde — power is *given* to them. [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/) | [https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary)

**Older Baptist (Gill):** Gill identifies the "western locusts" as the Roman Catholic clergy (cardinals, bishops, priests, monks, friars) and the "eastern locusts" as the Saracens (Arab Muslim armies). He notes an Arab tradition that locusts fell into Mahomet's hands with writing on their wings: "We are the army of the most high God." [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm)

---

### v. 4 — Protection of the Sealed; Only the Unsealed Are Harmed

**Traditional Reading:** The locusts are commanded not to harm vegetation but only "those men which have not the seal of God in their foreheads." This is a direct allusion to Revelation 7:3, where the 144,000 from the tribes of Israel are sealed. Those sealed are divinely protected. The Pulpit Commentary notes the seal may not be visible to men — it is God who knows His own (cf. 2 Tim. 2:19: "The Lord knoweth them that are his"). This teaches that God preserves His own even when it appears the innocent suffer with the guilty. [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/9-4.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/9-4.htm)

**Reformed Baptist (Fortner):** Fortner emphasizes that the seal is upon God's elect: "Those who trust the Lord Jesus Christ have the seal of God upon them." Even in the greatest tribulation, God's people are safe and secure — the judgments prove for their spiritual and eternal good (Rom. 8:28). [https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html)

**Baptist (Garner-Howes):** The sealed people are specifically "natural Israel only" — the 144,000 of Revelation 7:3–4. The seal is a "forehead mark" against death distinct from the sealing of the Holy Spirit upon all children of God. [https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/revelation-9.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/revelation-9.html)

---

### v. 5 — Torment for Five Months

**Traditional Reading:** The locusts are not permitted to kill, only to torment. The five-month period corresponds to the typical lifespan and active season of natural locusts (approximately May to September). Precept Austin explains: the torment serves a merciful purpose — keeping people alive so they have opportunity to repent. If Satan had his way, he would kill the unregenerate to prevent their repentance, but God limits the demons as He limited Satan regarding Job (Job 2:6). The torment is likened to a scorpion sting, which is excruciating but rarely fatal. [https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary) | [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

**Older Baptist (Gill):** In Gill's reading, the five months are not literal but represent the duration of Saracen power or papal oppression. He notes that from Mahomet's public preaching (AD 612) to the building of Baghdad (AD 762) when the Saracens settled was exactly 150 years — "five months of years" in prophetic reckoning. [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm)

---

### v. 6 — Men Seek Death but Cannot Die

**Traditional Reading:** The torment is so severe that men actively seek death — but death "flees from them." Enduring Word notes this is a demonic deception: the tormented want death as Paul did (Phil. 1:21–23) but for an entirely different reason. For Paul, death meant being with Christ; for these, death would be leaping from present torment into eternal fire. The commentary references the Columbine killers as a modern example: believing death would take them to "a better place" while planning murder. The point is that now is the time for repentance — death offers no escape from spiritual reality. [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

**Baptist (MacArthur):** MacArthur says simply: "Death has taken a holiday. There will be no escape from the agony inflicted by the demons, no escape from divine judgment. All attempts at suicide will fail." [https://www.gty.org/sermons/81-179/unleashing-hell-on-earth](https://www.gty.org/sermons/81-179/unleashing-hell-on-earth)

---

### vv. 7–10 — The Appearance of the Demonic Locusts

**Traditional Reading:** The repeated use of "like" (horses, gold, men's faces, women's hair, lions' teeth) signals that these are not literal descriptions but visionary depictions of demonic beings. Enduring Word quotes Walvoord: "A visual representation of the hordes of demons loosed upon the earth." Henry Morris suggests God has created bodies for these long-imprisoned spirits — "bodies appropriate in demonic appearance to the character of the demonic inhabitants." The sound "like chariots" echoes Joel 2:5. Popular speculations that these describe helicopter gunships are "interesting, but purely speculative." [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

**Pentecostal/Charismatic (Enduring Word, David Guzik):** Guzik, who pastors a Calvary Chapel (charismatic-leaning), takes a consistently futurist, literal-demonic view. He explicitly rejects both the historicist identification (Saracens, Turks, monks) and the modern-warfare speculation (helicopters). For Guzik, these are actual demonic beings released in a future Great Tribulation. [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

**Baptist (Garner-Howes):** Takes a straightforward futurist view: the locusts are demonic beings, not natural insects. The description is John's attempt to convey in human language the horrifying appearance of these creatures. [https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/revelation-9.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/revelation-9.html)

---

### v. 11 — Abaddon / Apollyon

**Traditional Reading:** The demonic locusts have a king, which distinguishes them from natural locusts (Proverbs 30:27: "the locusts have no king"). The king is "the angel of the Abyss," named *Abaddon* in Hebrew and *Apollyon* in Greek — both meaning "destruction" or "destroyer." Most interpreters see this as Satan himself or a very high-ranking demonic prince. Enduring Word notes: "This is obviously Satan himself or another high-ranking leader of demons." [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

**Reformed Baptist (MacArthur):** MacArthur does not dogmatically identify Abaddon as Satan but notes that the name means "destroyer," fitting the nature of this being. The Abyss is where certain demons are held in chains, and this being rules over them. [https://www.gty.org/sermons/81-179/unleashing-hell-on-earth](https://www.gty.org/sermons/81-179/unleashing-hell-on-earth)

**Older Baptist (Gill):** In Gill's historicist reading, the king over the locusts represents the Pope (over the western locusts) or Mahomet (over the eastern locusts) — both "destroyers" of souls. [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm)

---

### v. 12 — The First Woe Is Past

**Traditional Reading:** This is a transitional verse marking that the fifth trumpet (the first of the three "woes" announced in Rev. 8:13) has been described. Two more woes are to come — the sixth and seventh trumpets. Precept Austin notes that the second woe brings a demonic army unseen before, and the third woe (the seventh trumpet) brings the seven bowl judgments. [https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary)

**Anglican (Ellicott):** Ellicott observes: "Here is the patience and faith of the saints. The troubles which pass only yield place to more, the rest and the victory are not yet; the powers of evil have not exhausted themselves." [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/9-12.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/9-12.htm)

---

### v. 13 — The Voice from the Golden Altar

**Traditional Reading:** The sixth trumpet sounds, and John hears a voice from the four horns of the golden altar before God. This is the altar of incense, representing the prayers of God's people. Enduring Word notes: "In this, John recalled a repeated theme: the prayers of God's people play a large role in the end-times drama." The horns were where atoning blood was applied. The voice likely comes from God or from the prayers of the martyrs (cf. Rev. 6:9–10), connecting vengeance to intercession. [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

---

### vv. 14–15 — Release of the Four Angels at the Euphrates

**Traditional Reading:** The sixth angel is commanded to release four angels "bound at the great river Euphrates." These are prepared for a specific "hour and day and month and year" — emphasizing God's precise sovereign timing. They are released to kill a third of mankind, a far deadlier mission than the torment-only mandate of the locusts. The Euphrates is significant as the boundary of the land promised to Israel (Gen. 15:18), the frontier of the old Roman Empire, and the site of several primeval events: the first sin (Eden's river), the first murder (Cain fled east of Eden), the first organized rebellion (Babel), and the first war confederation (Gen. 14). Enduring Word notes the four angels are "probably evil angels" who are "servants of the divine purpose." [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/) | [https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary)

**Reformed Baptist (Fortner):** Fortner interprets the sixth trumpet broadly as "not one particular war, but all wars, past, present, and future." The powers of evil are graciously restrained until God turns them loose to accomplish His purpose. The duration of wars and the damage they inflict are determined not by men but by God. [https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html)

---

### v. 16 — The 200 Million Horsemen

**Traditional Reading:** The number is 200 million (Greek: *dis myriades myriadōn*, "two myriads of myriads"). Enduring Word notes this may be symbolic — "an army that is impossible to count and is greater than anything mankind has ever seen." The total of all armies in World War II was only 70 million. Even if China's 1965 claimed militia of 200 million were credited, it is hard to see such an army killing a third of mankind. Therefore many commentators lean toward a demonic army rather than a human one. [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

---

### vv. 17–19 — Description of the Horses and Riders

**Traditional Reading:** The riders have breastplates of fire (red), hyacinth (blue), and sulfur (yellow) — colors associated with judgment. The horses have lion-like heads, and from their mouths come fire, smoke, and sulfur — the three plagues that kill a third of mankind. Enduring Word discusses two interpretive options: (a) John describes modern mechanized warfare in the only terms available to him (tanks, artillery, aircraft), or (b) this is a supernatural demonic army. The tails like serpents with heads that inflict harm suggest demonic powers attacking from every direction. The "safest interpretation" is to see this as a demonic army invading earth. [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

**Baptist (Garner-Howes):** Interestingly, Garner-Howes suggests the fire, smoke, and brimstone from the horses' mouths destroy the riders themselves: "The riders were or are destroyed by the very horses on which they ride into battle." The destruction comes from within — "Out of man's own carnal, corrupt, covetous body of self-will comes his own destruction." [https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/revelation-9.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/revelation-9.html)

---

### vv. 20–21 — Mankind Refuses to Repent

**Traditional Reading:** Despite the overwhelming judgments — demonic torment and the death of a third of humanity — the survivors do not repent. They continue worshiping demons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood (echoing Psalm 115:4–7 and Daniel 5:23). They also do not repent of murders, sorceries (*pharmakeia*, often associated with drug use), sexual immorality, and thefts. Enduring Word notes: "It is amazing to see how quickly things return to what is thought to be normal after some calamity." The purpose of the judgments was to bring repentance, but hardened hearts refuse. [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

**Reformed Baptist (Fortner):** Fortner draws a strong Calvinistic lesson: "All men are so obstinately sinful and rebellious that judgment alone will never bring them to repentance. 'It is the goodness of God that leadeth thee to repentance' (Rom. 2:4). Neither the threats of the law nor the terrors of wrath will produce true repentance, but the goodness of God revealed in the crucified Christ will." [https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html)

**Pentecostal/Charismatic (Precept Austin / Enduring Word):** Precept Austin observes God's "wry wit" in judgment: He unleashes upon the world the very demons they worship, so they "get a fill of their ways" — yet they still refuse to repent. The list of sins (murders, sorceries/drugs, sexual immorality, thefts) is "a striking accusation against our present age." [https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary) | [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

---

## Where Protestant Traditions Differ

### Historicist vs. Futurist Interpretation

The clearest divide in Revelation 9 is between **historicist** and **futurist** readings:

- **Historicist (older Baptist — Gill, some Reformed):** The locusts represent the Saracens and/or the Roman Catholic clergy. The five months represent 150 years (using "a day for a year" reckoning). The star is the Pope or Mahomet. The smoke is false doctrine (papal decrees, the Koran). This view was dominant among Protestant Reformers and early Baptists who saw the papacy as Antichrist. [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/revelation/9.htm)

- **Futurist (MacArthur/Baptist, Guzik/Pentecostal, Garner-Howes/Baptist, Precept Austin/Evangelical):** These events are future and belong to the Great Tribulation. The locusts are literal demonic beings; the judgments are supernatural. The star is Satan or a demonic prince. This is the dominant view among contemporary evangelicals, Baptists, and Pentecostals. [https://www.gty.org/sermons/81-179/unleashing-hell-on-earth](https://www.gty.org/sermons/81-179/unleashing-hell-on-earth) | [https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/](https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-9/)

- **Modified Historicist / Symbolic (Fortner, Reformed Baptist):** Fortner blends the visions into a general description of all wars and tribulations throughout the church age. The fifth trumpet represents "seasons of great apostasy in the world until Christ comes again." This is closer to an idealist/amillennial reading within a Reformed Baptist framework. [https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html)

### Who Are the Sealed?

- **Dispensational Baptist (Garner-Howes):** The sealed are specifically the 144,000 from natural Israel (Rev. 7:3–4). The church has already been raptured. The seal is a physical forehead mark protecting from death. [https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/revelation-9.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/ghb/revelation-9.html)

- **Reformed Baptist (Fortner):** The sealed are all God's elect — "those who trust the Lord Jesus Christ have the seal of God upon them." It is spiritual, not ethnic. [https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html)

- **Anglican (Pulpit Commentary):** The seal may not be visible to man — it is God's knowledge of His own, possibly related to baptismal sealing (cf. Eph. 1:13; 4:30). [https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/9-4.htm](https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/9-4.htm)

### The Purpose of the Judgments

- **Reformed / Calvinist (Fortner):** The judgments do not and cannot produce repentance — only God's goodness in Christ does. The passage demonstrates total depravity: not even hell on earth brings repentance. [https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html](https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/fdc/revelation-9.html)

- **Arminian-leaning (Precept Austin, Enduring Word):** The judgments are designed by God to give opportunity for repentance. God mercifully restrains the demons from killing precisely so people can repent. The failure to repent is a real choice, not a decree. [https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary](https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-9-commentary)

## Other Views

### Modern Scholarship

The NET Bible notes (netbible.org) were not successfully fetched due to search constraints. However, the search results listed the site as a resource for modern scholarship on Revelation 9.

### Catholic / Orthodox

No Catholic or Orthodox commentary pages were successfully accessed within the fetch limit. The search results listed newadvent.org, catholic.com, and oca.org as available sources. These would typically offer a reading compatible with amillennial or idealist frameworks, though specific content could not be confirmed.

### Preterist Reading

Mark Copeland's study guide (ccel.org) offers a preterist-leaning Churches of Christ perspective: the visions reminded John's original readers that their oppressors ("those who do not have the seal of God") would face God's wrath, giving hope to persecuted first-century Christians. Content was limited in the excerpts. [https://ccel.org/contrib/exec_outlines/rev/rev_09.htm](https://ccel.org/contrib/exec_outlines/rev/rev_09.htm)
